column1: # THE FORTY-FOUR BOROUGHS LAID AGAINST THE HOUSEHOLDS — AND THERE ARE FORTY-SEVEN OF THEM.
# Row 260. Berliner Adressbuch (ZLB, PI 34115495) householder runs 1938-1943, read at the page
# image, laid beside the Bundesarchiv Gedenkbuch's Berlin Leibholz in data/leibholz-gedenkbuch.tsv.
# Read 11 October 2026.
# WHAT THIS ROW WAS WAITING FOR, AND THE FACT THAT IT WAS NOT WAITING FOR ANYTHING.
# On 22 September a text-layer pass concluded that "the borough matching needs the page images for

column1: # ---------------- THE RE-READING, AND WHAT IT CHANGES ----------------
FOUR VOLUMES RE-READ AT THE IMAGE, AND ALL FOUR COUNTS HOLD
column2: 1939 ELEVEN · 1941 NINE · 1942 SIX · 1943 FOUR, each run bounded above by the headword "Leibholz s. a. Leipholz" and below by the next surname (Leibich in 1942 and 1943, Leibich/Leibig either side in 1941). Every forename in the 20 September list is in the 11 October reading and no forename is in one and not the other. THIS IS A REPLICATION, NOT A NEW FIND, and it is worth the hour because the whole borough argument rests on these six lists.

column1: where the runs physically are, for whoever reads them next
column2: 1939 p1719 (printed 1683), the whole run in column 4, the last column · 1941 p1795, SPLIT ACROSS A COLUMN BREAK — the headword and two entries at the foot of column 3, the remaining seven at the head of column 4 under a repeated headword · 1942 p1776, column 3, with a repeated headword MID-COLUMN after the first entry · 1943 p1744, column 3. THE PAGES ARE FOUR COLUMNS WIDE, NOT FIVE, which is worth knowing before cropping.

column1: *** AND THE TEXT LAYER IS NOT AS BLIND AS 22 SEPTEMBER CONCLUDED ***
column2: the 1942 and 1943 runs come out of the per-page OCR endpoint essentially intact and agree with the image line for line. What fails is SEARCHING for the surname, because the headword is mangled; what works is pulling the whole page's text and reading the run in place. 1941 genuinely cannot be read that way — the OCR interleaves columns 3 and 4 there and silently attributes nine LEIBNITZ entries to Leibholz. A method that cannot tell those apart is not a method, which is why all four were read at the image anyway.

column1: # ---------------- FOUR DETAILS THE 20 SEPTEMBER LIST DOES NOT CARRY ----------------
1939 WITH ITS TRADES AND STREET NUMBERS, WHICH IS WHAT THE BOROUGH WORK NEEDS
column2: Albert Möbel Halensee Westfälische Str 66 T. · C Kaufm N65 Afrikanische Str 37 · Ella Krankenschwest Schönebg Reppichstraße 28 T. · Felix Pensionär NW40 Scharnhorststr 25 · Fritz kfm Angest Schönebg Geßlerstr 15 · Georg Wäscherei SO16 Michaelkirchstr 26 · Heinrich Buchführ Neukölln Leinestr 32 · Helmut Bankbeamt Schmargendf Dievenowstr 19 · Jaques Kaufm Schönebg Meraner Str 2 T. · Peter Fabrikbes Grunewald Joseph-Joachim-Straße 35 T. · Wilhelm Vertret NO18 Weinstr 6.

column1: *** PETER DID NOT STAY A FABRIKDIREKTOR AND DID NOT STAY IN DRAKESTRASSE ***
column2: 1938 gives "Peter, Fabrikdirektor, W35 Drakestr 1". 1939 gives "Peter Fabrikbes Grunewald Joseph-Joachim-Straße 35 T." — read at four times magnification, the word is FABRIKBES, Fabrikbesitzer, A FACTORY OWNER, not a director. He moved from Tiergarten to Grunewald and from employee to proprietor IN 1939, which is the wrong direction for a Jewish businessman in that year and is one reason to doubt that he was one. He carries no Israel in any volume and he is in no Gedenkbuch entry.

column1: ALBERT CHANGED TRADE IN THE SAME YEAR
column2: 1938 "Antiquitäten", 1939 "Möbel" — antiques to furniture, same house, Westfälische Straße 66 in Halensee. He sailed for Shanghai on 27 June 1939 and died there on 18 August 1944, so the 1939 volume is the last that holds him and it holds him under a changed trade.

column1: AND WILHELM OF WEINSTRASSE 6 WAS DEMOTED A YEAR EARLIER THAN THIS ARCHIVE SAID
column2: data/berlin-adressbuch-names.tsv dates his fall "1940 to 1941", Vertreter to Bauarbeiter. THE FIRST STEP IS 1938 TO 1939: Kaufmann in 1938, VERTRETER in 1939, Vertreter in 1940, Bauarbeiter in 1941. A merchant became a commercial traveller, then a building labourer, in three printed volumes. The 1940-41 step is the one the archive noticed because it is the one with "Israel" printed beside it; the 1938-39 step is just as real and has no marking on it at all.

column1: # ---------------- THE COUNT ROW 260 PROPOSED IS WRONG IN THREE PLACES ----------------
*** IT IS FORTY-SEVEN BERLIN RESIDENCES, NOT FORTY-FOUR ***
column2: counted from data/leibholz-gedenkbuch.tsv, all 52 rows: Schöneberg 6, Charlottenburg 5, Wilmersdorf 6, Friedrichshain 5, Mitte 4, Tiergarten 4, Neukölln 4, Prenzlauer Berg 3, Kreuzberg 1 — THIRTY-EIGHT with one borough; THREE with two boroughs (Hans, Laura née Rothenberg, Sophie née Rothenberg); FIVE with plain "Berlin" and no borough (Else née Soldin, Helene Kamnitzer, Willi, and the two LAIBHOLZ spellings, Georg and Lidia); and ONE with Berlin second after another town (Heinz Paul Hugo, "Paderborn (Umschulungslager Grüner Weg); Berlin (Neukölln)"). 38 + 3 + 5 + 1 = 47. FIVE of the fifty-two are not Berlin at all: two Hamburg, two Frankfurt, one Dortmund/Düsseldorf.

column1: and the row's own figures do not add up to its own total
column2: 6+6+5+5+4+4+4+3+1 = 38, plus three plain and two dual = 43, written as forty-four. The arithmetic was wrong before the data was. Corrected here rather than edited away.

column1: # ---------------- KREUZBERG: ONE PERSON, ONE HOUSEHOLD, AND THE METHOD WORKS ----------------
*** THE ONLY BOROUGH WHERE THE ARITHMETIC FORCES AN IDENTIFICATION ***
column2: Gedenkbuch Kreuzberg holds EXACTLY ONE Leibholz: SAMUEL, born 28 June 1877 at Schubin, murdered at Auschwitz 10 April 1943. The Adressbuch holds EXACTLY ONE Leibholz household in Kreuzberg: Samuel, Hüte en gros, SW68 Kommandantenstraße 29 — 1936, 1938, and then as "Israel, Hüte" at the same address in 1940 and 1941. One and one, and the forename agrees in the years before the decree. SAMUEL IS ALREADY ONE OF THE FOUR THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS, so this identifies nobody new; what it does is show that the instrument returns the right answer where the right answer is already known.

column1: # ---------------- TIERGARTEN: SIX NAMES ONTO ONE PRINTED LINE ----------------
FOUR OF THE SIX ARE ONE FLAT
column2: Gedenkbuch Tiergarten: Else née Seelig (b. 1889 Glowitz), Kurt, Lieselotte, Walter — plus Hans and Laura née Rothenberg, both recorded as Charlottenburg AND Tiergarten. The Adressbuch's Tiergarten householders are Hans Dr (W35 Graf-Spee-Str 4, 1938 only), Peter (W35 Drakestr 1, 1938 only) and "A ISRAEL, Fleischermeister, NW87 LEVETZOWSTRASSE 13" (1940) who becomes "A Israel, Arbeiter" at the same address in 1941. THE FOUR TIERGARTEN NAMES ARE THE LEVETZOWSTRASSE 13 HOUSEHOLD this archive already holds, and A. Israel is its householder. FOUR GEDENKBUCH NAMES ONTO ONE PRINTED LINE — which is exactly what row 260 said the method would buy, demonstrated once.

column1: *** AND HANS'S TWO BOROUGHS ARE A MOVE, WITH A DATE ON IT ***
column2: the Gedenkbuch gives Hans as "Berlin (Charlottenburg); Berlin (Tiergarten)" and says nothing about which came first. The Adressbuch has HANS DR AT W35 GRAF-SPEE-STRASSE 4 IN 1938, in Tiergarten, and the 1939 census has Hans of the Schlochau household at DANCKELMANNSTRASSE 44 IN CHARLOTTENBURG. So the order is TIERGARTEN 1938, CHARLOTTENBURG 1939 — a move in the year between, and the Gedenkbuch's unordered pair now has a direction. He was deported 12 January 1943 and dead at Auschwitz on 22 February. NOT PROVED that the 1938 Dr Hans and the 1939 Hans are one man; two Hans Leibholz in Berlin is possible and the Gedenkbuch's own dual borough is the reason to think they are not two.

column1: # ---------------- NEUKÖLLN: THE TRAP, SPRUNG, AND CAUGHT BY SOMETHING ELSE ----------------
TWO LEIBHOLZ HOUSEHOLDS IN ONE BOROUGH, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS IN THE GEDENKBUCH
column2: Adressbuch Neukölln holds HEINRICH (Verwaltungsbeamter, later Buchführer, LEINESTRASSE 32, in every volume 1938 to 1942) and the BUTCHER (Willi, Fleischermeister, KAISER-FRIEDRICH-STRASSE 59/60 in 1938; Wilhelm, Fleischermeister, LENAUSTRASSE 25 in 1940, 1941 and 1942). Gedenkbuch Neukölln holds Erna née Hammer, Johanna Simon née Leibholz, Ruth, Wilhelm, and Heinz Paul Hugo by way of Paderborn. THE BOROUGH ALONE CANNOT SAY WHICH HOUSEHOLD THEY BELONG TO. What says it is the trade and the marking: the butcher's household is the Stolp lane this archive already holds — Willi, Erna née Hammer and a son — and HEINRICH CARRIES NO "ISRAEL" IN ANY VOLUME AND IS STILL PRINTED IN 1942. A borough is a filter and not an identifier, and here is the case that proves it.

column1: *** AND THE BUTCHER'S HOUSEHOLD HAS AN ADDRESS THE LANE DOES NOT CARRY ***
column2: the register of lines begins the Stolp household at "Neukölln 1939, Lenaustraße 25". THE 1938 VOLUME PUTS HIM AT KAISER-FRIEDRICH-STRASSE 59/60, as Willi rather than Wilhelm. He is absent from the 1939 volume entirely and back at Lenaustraße 25 in 1940. So the household moved between 1938 and 1940 and the lane's start date is a volume late.

column1: and the Willi/Wilhelm question this archive raised is now answered by one page
column2: data/adressbuch-namenteil-runs.tsv asked whether the 1938 Willi of Kaiser-Friedrich-Straße and the 1940 Wilhelm of Lenaustraße were one man who moved, and declined to assert it. THE 1941 VOLUME PRINTS TWO WILHELMS ON CONSECUTIVE LINES — "Wilhelm Israel Bauarb NO18 Weinstr 6" and "Wilhelm Fleischermstr Neukölln Lenaustr 25 T." So there were certainly TWO men of that name in Berlin in 1941, one marked and one not, and the Neukölln butcher is not the Weinstraße man. THAT IS WHAT IS SETTLED. Whether the Neukölln butcher of 1940 is the Neukölln butcher of 1938 under a shortened forename is still an inference and is still not asserted.

column1: # ---------------- MITTE: THREE PEOPLE, ONE TRANSPORT, ONE DAY ----------------
THE BOROUGH CORROBORATES A FAMILY THE ARCHIVE BUILT FROM YAD VASHEM
column2: Gedenkbuch Mitte: Georg (b. 1884 Hammerstein), Lydia née Perl, Elli Struzik née Leibholz (b. 7 November 1915, BERLIN), Hedwig Nehemias née Leibholz, and Sophie née Rothenberg by way of Schöneberg. GEORG, LYDIA AND ELLI WERE ON THE SAME TRANSPORT — Berlin to Litzmannstadt, 1 November 1941 — AND DIED AT CHELMNO ON THE SAME DAY, 13 MAY 1942. The Adressbuch's Mitte householder for that household is "Georg, Wäscherei, SO16 MICHAELKIRCHSTRASSE 26", present 1938 and 1939 and gone from 1940. Elli as Georg's daughter is this archive's existing reading from the Pages of Testimony; the borough, the transport and the death date agree with it and were arrived at independently.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT THE METHOD CANNOT DO, STATED PLAINLY ----------------
IT CANNOT TOUCH SCHÖNEBERG, CHARLOTTENBURG, WILMERSDORF, FRIEDRICHSHAIN OR PRENZLAUER BERG
column2: those five boroughs hold TWENTY-FIVE of the forty-seven, and the Adressbuch holds between zero and three Leibholz households in each — CHARLOTTENBURG FIVE PEOPLE AND NO HOUSEHOLD AT ALL, PRENZLAUER BERG THREE PEOPLE AND NO HOUSEHOLD AT ALL. People who lived in a flat somebody else rented are not householders and are not in the Namenteil. A borough with five dead and no printed household is not a failure of the reading; it is the shape of the source.

column1: AND THE FOURTEEN MARRIED SURNAMES ARE WHERE IT WAS ALWAYS GOING TO BREAK
column2: the row hoped a borough plus a maiden name would find the household a woman left. IT FINDS A BOROUGH SHE DIED FROM, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT THING — Dorothea Dukelsky née Leibholz is recorded at Schöneberg in 1942, and the Schöneberg Leibholz households are Jaques at Meraner Straße 2, Ella at Reppichstraße 28 and Fritz at Geßlerstraße 15, none of which is where a married woman of sixty-three was living. NO MATCH IS MADE ON THAT BASIS HERE AND NONE SHOULD BE.

column1: *** THE HONEST YIELD, COUNTED ***
column2: FORTY-SEVEN Berlin Gedenkbuch people. The method attaches FOUR to one printed household (Levetzowstraße 13), CORROBORATES THREE already attached (Michaelkirchstraße 26), CONFIRMS ONE already known (Samuel at Kommandantenstraße 29), and PUTS A DIRECTION ON ONE unordered pair of boroughs (Hans, Tiergarten then Charlottenburg). THE OTHER THIRTY-EIGHT IT DOES NOT TOUCH. That is the measurement row 260 asked for, and the number that matters is thirty-eight.

column1: nothing here is a new person
column2: every Gedenkbuch name above was already in data/leibholz-gedenkbuch.tsv and every Adressbuch household was already in data/berlin-adressbuch-names.tsv. What is new is which belongs with which, and three corrections to this archive's own figures.
